Sats is the smallest unit of bitcoin, equal to one hundred millionth of a bitcoin. Sats is used in bitcoin communities to refer to small amounts of value. Sats is a term that can appear in discussions of bitcoin transactions.

KYC stands for Know Your Customer. KYC is an identity verification process required by many regulated financial service providers. KYC requires users to submit personal identification details before they can use a service.

ICO stands for initial coin offering. ICO is a fundraising method in which a project sells newly issued tokens to investors. ICO is associated in community warnings with risks of fraud and with projects that do not deliver what they promise.

Shill is slang for promoting a cryptocurrency or project. Shill is used to accuse a person of promoting an asset while concealing a financial interest in it. Shill is often directed at promotional posts in forums and social media.

Pump signals are messages urging others to buy an asset so that its price rises. Pump signals are shared in forums and social media channels. Pump signals are often linked to pump-and-dump schemes in which early holders sell after the price has risen.
